rtc-01-c1.text: Institute for New Testament Textual Research (INTF), University of Münster (n.d.). The Coherence-Based Genealogical Method. INTF website.
rtc-01-c1.quote: Most of the 5,700 extant manuscripts were copied in the second millennium.
rtc-01-c1.claim: The Institute for New Testament Textual Research (INTF) in Münster puts the extant Greek manuscripts at about 5,700, most of them copied in the second millennium.

rtc-01-c1.text: Center for the Study of New Testament Manuscripts (interview with Peter J. Gurry) (2019). Interviews With the Authors: Myths and Mistakes, Peter J. Gurry. CSNTM.
rtc-01-c1.quote: For the sake of my own estimate (which is about ½ million), I defined a “variant” as a non-spelling difference in wording in our Greek manuscripts.
rtc-01-c1.claim: He counted every difference in wording among Greek manuscripts, ignoring spelling, and arrived at roughly half a million.

rtc-01-c1.text: Peter J. Gurry (2016). The Number of Variants in the Greek New Testament: A Proposed Estimate. New Testament Studies.
rtc-01-c1.quote: Proper use shows that the number reflects the frequency with which scribes copied more than their infidelity in doing so.
rtc-01-c1.claim: Gurry argues that the total reflects how often the text was copied more than how carelessly it was copied.

rtc-01-c1.text: Institute for New Testament Textual Research (INTF), University of Münster (n.d.). The Coherence-Based Genealogical Method. INTF website.
rtc-01-c1.quote: A significant split of the tradition occurs in about ten percent of the variation units.
rtc-01-c1.claim: in most places only one or a few manuscripts stray from a reliable majority, and a significant split in the tradition occurs in about ten per cent of the variation units

rtc-01-c2.quote: repeating the same word twice (dittography), omitting one of two similar adjacent letters or words (haplography), and missing words or lines because the same word occurs further on in a passage (homoioteleuton)
rtc-01-c2.claim: missing words or lines because the same word occurs further on

rtc-01-c2.text: Institute for New Testament Textual Research (INTF), University of Münster (n.d.). The Coherence-Based Genealogical Method. INTF website.
rtc-01-c2.quote: The early church father Jerome even complains that they often did not copy the text as it stood in their exemplars but rather as they understood it.
rtc-01-c2.claim: The INTF recalls that Jerome complained that scribes often copied the text not as it stood in their exemplars but as they understood it

rtc-01-c2.text: John L. Cisne, Robert M. Ziomkowski, Steven J. Schwager (2010). Mathematical Philology: Entropy Information in Refining Classical Texts' Reconstruction, and Early Philologists' Anticipation of Information Theory. PLoS ONE.
rtc-01-c2.quote: scribal errors tend to replace less frequent and hence entropically more information-rich wordings with more frequent ones
rtc-01-c2.claim: They argued that scribal errors tend to replace rarer, more information-rich words with commoner ones, which is exactly the habit the rule assumes.

rtc-01-c2.text: John L. Cisne, Robert M. Ziomkowski, Steven J. Schwager (2010). Mathematical Philology: Entropy Information in Refining Classical Texts' Reconstruction, and Early Philologists' Anticipation of Information Theory. PLoS ONE.
rtc-01-c2.quote: in agreement with the P2 = 547/756 = 0.72±0.03 (95% confidence interval) fraction of Lachmann's choices taken to be correct by Ernout
rtc-01-c2.claim: a later edition by Ernout accepted 547 of them, or 72 per cent

rtc-01-c3.text: Barbara Bordalejo (2006). Textual Scholarship: Stemmatics. textualscholarship.org.
rtc-01-c3.quote: The Lachmann method, as formulated by Paul Maas, uses common errors in manuscripts to determine if they are or are not related
rtc-01-c3.claim: The method as formulated by Maas uses common errors to decide whether manuscripts are related

rtc-01-c3.text: Barbara Bordalejo (2006). Textual Scholarship: Stemmatics. textualscholarship.org.
rtc-01-c3.quote: One of the strongest arguments against the method was advanced by Giorgio Pasquali, who especially disagreed with the supposition that every textual tradition must descend from a single archetype
rtc-01-c3.claim: One of the strongest objections came from Giorgio Pasquali, who disagreed with the supposition that every textual tradition must descend from a single archetype and showed how little the method achieves when applied strictly.

rtc-01-c3.text: Peter J. Gurry (2017). A Critical Examination of the Coherence-Based Genealogical Method in the Catholic Epistles. Tyndale Bulletin.
rtc-01-c3.quote: because it was designed to address the problems of textual contamination and coincidental agreement, the CBGM has significance far beyond the confines of biblical studies
rtc-01-c3.claim: Peter Gurry notes that the method was designed to address contamination and coincidental agreement, and it has become an essential tool for the editors of the standard Greek New Testament.

rtc-01-c3.text: Katarzyna Anna Kapitan (2025). A digital perspective on the role of a stemma in material-philological transmission studies. arXiv.
rtc-01-c3.quote: allows us to view the stemma codicum as a research tool rather than the final product of our scholarly investigation
rtc-01-c3.claim: Katarzyna Kapitan argues that this lets us treat the stemma as a research tool rather than the final product of an edition

rtc-02-c1.quote: It follows, therefore, that the use of the vowel and accentuation signs was not instituted before the sixth century.
rtc-02-c1.claim: concludes that these signs were not introduced before the sixth century

rtc-02-c1.claim: The scribe Shlomo ben Buya'a copied the consonants, and Aharon ben Asher, the most outstanding of the Masoretes of Tiberias, added the vowels, accents and notes.

rtc-02-c1.text: Paul Sanders (2015). Review of Matti Friedman, The Aleppo Codex. Review of Biblical Literature.

rtc-02-c1.claim: written in 1009, whose vowels were adjusted to Ben Asher's system, as its colophon states

rtc-02-c2.claim: 72 translators sent from Jerusalem to Alexandria produced the Greek Pentateuch in the reign of Ptolemy II Philadelphus (285–246 BCE)

rtc-02-c2.claim: The Septuagint version is one-eighth shorter than the Masoretic one.

rtc-02-c2.claim: together with the Greek New Testament it is still the official Bible of the Greek Orthodox Church

rtc-02-c3.claim: The first copy to reach Western scholars was obtained in Damascus by Pietro della Valle in 1616, and hopes ran high that it would reveal a text older than the MT.

rtc-02-c3.quote: Gesenius listed and analyzed the roughly 6,000 textual differences in terms of eight categories or classes

rtc-02-c3.claim: it is generally agreed that this was inserted to support the claim that Gerizim is "the chosen place"

rtc-02-c3.claim: Among the Dead Sea Scrolls, some biblical fragments clearly resemble the Samaritan text-type.

rtc-03-c1.claim: In late 1946 or in 1947, three Bedouin wandering along the north-west shore of the Dead Sea stumbled on a cave containing ten jars.

rtc-03-c1.text: Israel Antiquities Authority (n.d.). Introduction. The Leon Levy Dead Sea Scrolls Digital Library.

rtc-03-c1.claim: copies of books now in the Hebrew Bible, and every book is represented except Esther

rtc-03-c2.text: Israel Antiquities Authority (n.d.). Introduction. The Leon Levy Dead Sea Scrolls Digital Library.
rtc-03-c2.quote: This similarity is quite remarkable, considering that the Qumran Scrolls are over a thousand years older than previously identified biblical manuscripts.
rtc-03-c2.claim: Many biblical manuscripts closely resemble the Masoretic Text, which is remarkable given that they are over a thousand years older than any biblical manuscript known before.

rtc-03-c2.text: Israel Antiquities Authority (n.d.). Introduction. The Leon Levy Dead Sea Scrolls Digital Library.

rtc-03-c2.claim: some contain additions and deletions suggesting that their scribes felt free to modify what they copied

rtc-03-c2.claim: Lawrence Schiffman notes that the historian Josephus knew the passage, so it was at least part of some Jews' text of Samuel in Second Temple times, and he thinks it may belong to the original book.

rtc-03-c3.text: Israel Antiquities Authority (n.d.). Introduction. The Leon Levy Dead Sea Scrolls Digital Library.
rtc-03-c3.quote: The idea of a closed biblical “canon” only emerged later in the history of these sacred writings.
rtc-03-c3.claim: The Israel Antiquities Authority notes that the communities behind the scrolls had no unified idea of an authoritative collection of scriptures; the notion of a closed biblical canon emerged later.

rtc-03-c3.text: William Brent Seales, Clifford Seth Parker, Michael Segal, Emanuel Tov, Pnina Shor, Yosef Porath (2016). From damage to discovery via virtual unwrapping: Reading the scroll from En-Gedi. Science Advances.

rtc-03-c3.claim: Even the proto-Masoretic text still shows some fluidity in Judean Desert manuscripts from the first centuries CE, and only afterwards does a single consonantal text prevail.

rtc-04-c1.claim: When Peter Gurry wrote in 2016, the official Münster list held 127 papyri, 286 majuscules, 2,841 minuscules and 2,384 lectionaries.

rtc-07-c2.text: William Brent Seales, Clifford Seth Parker, Michael Segal, Emanuel Tov, Pnina Shor, Yosef Porath (2016). From damage to discovery via virtual unwrapping: Reading the scroll from En-Gedi. Science Advances.
rtc-07-c2.quote: the ink response within the micro-CT scan is denser than other materials, implying that it likely contains metal, such as iron or lead.
rtc-07-c2.claim: The ink showed up because it was denser than the parchment, which suggests it contains a metal such as iron or lead, although its exact composition is unknown because no exposed ink could be sampled.

rtc-07-c2.text: William Brent Seales, Clifford Seth Parker, Michael Segal, Emanuel Tov, Pnina Shor, Yosef Porath (2016). From damage to discovery via virtual unwrapping: Reading the scroll from En-Gedi. Science Advances.
rtc-07-c2.quote: Radiocarbon results date the scroll to the third or fourth century CE (table S1).
rtc-07-c2.claim: Radiocarbon dating places it in the third or fourth century CE, while the palaeographer Yardeni suggested the first or second century on the basis of the handwriting.

rtc-07-c2.text: William Brent Seales, Clifford Seth Parker, Michael Segal, Emanuel Tov, Pnina Shor, Yosef Porath (2016). From damage to discovery via virtual unwrapping: Reading the scroll from En-Gedi. Science Advances.
rtc-07-c2.quote: The text deciphered thus far is completely identical with the consonantal framework of the medieval text of the Hebrew Bible, traditionally named the Masoretic Text
rtc-07-c2.claim: As far as it has been deciphered, its text is completely identical with the consonantal framework of the medieval Masoretic Text.
